id: title:Gilbert09:pace github page fetches against the egress budget

review.posthog_relevance: GitHub connector implementation, specifically GitHub Enterprise installation rate-limiting and worker-drain compatibility.
review.reason: The change implements GitHub Enterprise installation-specific rate-limiting and worker-drain compatibility. P1.F3.H4 and P1.F3.H5 show the implementation of a wait-before-request mechanism and worker-shutdown-aware waiting, while P1.F1.H1 and P1.F2.H6 show the helper and query changes. This is a substantive, bounded capability improvement.
review.uncertainty: The tier depends on the underlying rate-limiting and worker-drain mechanisms being established and safe, which are not fully demonstrated in this chunk. observations.posthog_connection: Paces GitHub API calls for a given installation and resource, returning seconds to wait before the next call. This could help avoid rate-limiting when bulk importing or syncing GitHub data, allowing callers to wait rather than be shed.

observations.behavior: Adds a wait before requesting GitHub API, gated by an installation-specific pace and a global retry-after ceiling.
observations.posthog_connection: Checks if an installation exists, then calls a new pacing function before making the request; this could prevent a long-running backfill from exhausting the shared egress budget and being shed.

observations.behavior: Implements the pacing and worker-drain-aware wait, choosing between a sleep and a worker-shutdown event wait.
observations.posthog_connection: Uses the worker activity to wait for shutdown rather than sleeping, allowing the pod to drain while the request waits, and respects a global retry-after ceiling.
